findings.summary: The fix at 9dbf12f resolves the major finding from review 2. revalidate() now returns early while suppressRestore is set, so a passive focus, pageshow or visibility check no longer sends a request or changes the phase. A failed explicit logout therefore stays in 'error' and keeps its Sign out button, and the Retry session check button is hidden. The original fix still holds: a passive check does not POST logout, so it cannot revoke a newer session that shares the cookie. The expanded React/HTTP/PGlite test checks every point review 2 asked for. It injects the failure in the wrapped access.logout, before the server sets any cookie (server/adult-http.mjs:112-113), so the server session really does stay active. It then confirms that only an explicit retry revokes the session. Explicit logout, the late-response logout in verify(), server policy, scope and the open gates are unchanged. The controller's 61/61 tests, build, card check and source-bound run of all 8 native scenarios at 9dbf12f support the claims. The remaining issues are small edge cases.

findings.title: Back to request after a failed logout leaves no in-tab sign-out retry
findings.problem: If an explicit logout fails, the error state correctly keeps Sign out. But if the user clicks 'Back to request', the phase becomes 'request' while suppressRestore stays true and the server session is still active (verified in the test). The request phase has no Sign out control, and passive checks are now suppressed. So, unlike the 606e8c5 behaviour, the tab offers no way to retry the logout, even though the error text told the user to retry before leaving a shared browser. Reloading restores the restricted view, and Sign out can be retried from there. There is no false 'Signed out' confirmation, so this is a gap in recovery, not a false success.
findings.fix_check: Do one of the following. Option 1: track a 'logoutUnconfirmed' flag and keep an explicit Sign out (or a warning) visible in the request phase until a logout succeeds. Option 2: state in ADULT_ACCESS_CONTRACT.md that after Back the only recovery is to reload and sign out explicitly.

findings.title: suppressRestore is cleared only by a successful verify
findings.problem: After any explicit sign-out, the flag stays set until verification succeeds in this same tab (or the page reloads). If a later verify in this tab succeeds on the server but its response fails (verify's catch block → error), the Retry session check button is hidden and passive checks are skipped. The tab then cannot discover its own new session until the user reloads. This does not grant or reveal access, so the impact is limited to usability.
findings.fix_check: Optional: clear suppressRestore when a new request/verify attempt starts, or document that a reload is needed in this case.
